Match that pattern when reproducing CI locally.\n\n## Architecture\n\n### Workspace layout\n\n- `apps/` — Next.js apps. Each is an independently deployable Cloud Run service with its own `next.config.js`, `middleware.ts`, Sentry config, and `project.json`. Apps include `dashboard` (defaultProject), `fleet`, `route-planner` (legacy), `route-planner-v2` (current), `route-planner-viewer`, `billing`, `iam`, `iam-frontend`, `geocode`, `geofence-tool`, `live-tracking`, `map-editor`, `road-editor`, `nav-sdk-config`, `demo`, `share`.\n- `libs/` — Shared libraries. **Always import via TS path aliases**, not relative paths across project boundaries. From `tsconfig.base.json`:\n  - `@ncc/ui`, `@ncc/ui/client`, `@ncc/ui/server` — non-business primitives\n  - `@ncc/icons`, `@ncc/icons/common`, `@ncc/icons/navigation`\n  - `@ncc/common`, plus subpath entrypoints `client`, `edge`, `server`, `types`, `utils` — business components used across most apps. **Honor the entrypoint split**: server-only code must not be imported from a client subpath (and vice versa); pulling from `@ncc/common` directly drags everything.\n  - `@ncc/map`, `@ncc/optimization`, `@ncc/geocode-common`, `@ncc/route-planner-components`, `@ncc/telematics-hub`, `@ncc/animation`, `@ncc/playground`\n- `tools/` — Build/CDN/preview/release tooling (not a publishable package).\n- `docs/` — Internal design + ops docs. Read `docs/01 - dev setup.md` first when bootstrapping. Other docs cover specific features (route planner v2 architecture, preview deployments, release flow, qualified-tag workflow, etc.) — skim the index by filename rather than reading them all.\n\n### Apps depend on libs, libs do not depend on apps\n\n`nx.json` enables `@nx/enforce-module-boundaries`; an app may import any lib, but circular or app→lib boundary violations will fail lint. The `production` named input excludes `*.spec.*`, `*.stories.*`, storybook config, and eslint config from build inputs, which keeps the Nx cache stable.\n\n### Service topology (local dev)\n\n`docs/01 - dev setup.md`: NCC apps → BFF → Waymor → {Tokamak, Postgres}. The DB lives in a remote k8s cluster reached via `kubectl port-forward svc/waymer-db-stg -n platform 5432:5432`. You can't fully run NCC against live data without BFF + Waymor + a DB tunnel. For pure frontend changes, pointing an app at staging BFF (`.env.stg`) is usually enough.\n\n### Deployment topology\n\n- **Staging**: every push to `main` triggers `.github/workflows/main.yml` → builds nx-affected apps → uploads to GCS CDN + artifact → deploys.\n- **Production**: tag a SHA on `main` with `vX.Y.Z` and publish a GitHub Release → `.github/workflows/release.yml` builds and deploys per-app. **Single-branch model** — there is no `main → release` promote PR. Use `tools/release/` scripts (see below), not the GitHub UI.\n- **PR previews**: every PR builds affected apps as Docker images and deploys to Cloud Run at `console-preview-<app>-<suffix>-<hash>-<region>.a.run.app`. Local: `yarn preview:deploy <app> <suffix>` / `yarn preview:teardown <app> <suffix>`. Details in `docs/09 - preview deployments.md`.\n\n### Release flow (do NOT free-hand this)\n\nThe `.cursor/skills/ncc-release/SKILL.md` is the canonical playbook — read it before running any release. Summary:\n\n```\nmain ── pick SHA ──▶ git tag v1.3.N ──▶ gh release publish ──▶ release.yml ──▶ prod\n```\n\nScripts under `tools/release/` (all default to **dry-run**; require `--execute` to mutate):\n\n| Script | Purpose |\n|---|---|\n| `release-preflight.sh` | Sanity checks; exit `1` hard fail, `2` warnings (rerun with `--allow-warnings`) |\n| `next-version.sh` | Compute next `v1.3.N` from latest tag |\n| `compute-affected-apps.sh` | App list for the Release `name` field |\n| `generate-notes.sh` | Conventional-commit grouped notes |\n| `hotfix-from-tag.sh` | Cut a hotfix branch from a prior prod tag (when `main` has unshipped work) |\n| `create-github-release.sh` | Tag + publish + watch `release.yml`; auto-opens backport PR for hotfixes |\n\n**Hotfix invariant**: every hotfix tag must be reconciled to `main` either by reachability or a merged `[backport] vX.Y.Z` PR. Until then, `release-preflight.sh` hard-fails with `un-backported hotfix tag(s)`. Don't override with `--allow-orphan-tags` unless the user explicitly authorizes it.\n\nIf `gh` is not authenticated, **stop and run `gh auth login` first** — partial GitHub visibility makes preflight/orphan-tag logic unreliable.\n\n### Gotchas in release deploy matchers\n\n`release.yml` matches affected apps by substring. `route-planner` is a substring of `route-planner-v2` and `route-planner-viewer`. The v2 overlap is handled with `&& !contains(name, 'route-planner-v2')`, but **`route-planner-viewer` is not** — if the affected list contains `route-planner-viewer` without `route-planner`, `docker-route-planner` will still fire. Same caveat with `iam` ⊂ `iam-frontend`. The release scripts preserve this behavior; don't try to fix it incidentally as part of an unrelated change.\n\n## Linting / formatting\n\n- ESLint is wired through `@nx/eslint` with the `@nx/enforce-module-boundaries` rule on. Use `nx lint <project>` / `nx affected --target=lint`.\n- Prettier (`.prettierrc`): single quotes, no semicolons, `bracketSpacing: false`, trailing commas. Husky runs Prettier on staged `.ts(x)` automatically.\n- A `biome.json` exists with similar settings but **Biome is not wired into the Husky hook or Nx targets** — Prettier + ESLint are the source of truth for now.\n\n## Conventions worth knowing\n\n- **defaultProject** is `dashboard` (so bare `nx serve` / `nx build` target it).\n- `mapbox-gl` is explicitly stubbed out (`\"mapbox-gl\": \"npm:empty-npm-package@1.0.0\"`) — all map code uses `maplibre-gl` / `@nbai/nbmap-gl`. Don't add `mapbox-gl` imports.\n- Sentry is configured per-app via `sentry.*.config.ts` and `instrumentation*.ts`. Don't add a global Sentry init.\n- `nx.json` sets `neverConnectToCloud: true` and `useInferencePlugins: false`. There is an `nxCloudAccessToken` for CI cache reads, but local runs stay offline.\n- `tools/sync/` and `.github/workflows/sync-release-to-main.yml` are **frozen MVP artifacts from an earlier dual-branch attempt**. Leave them alone; they're not part of the current flow.\n"

### CLAUDE (2026-05-28T12:20:59.114Z)

The install reached the Link step where Yarn runs each package's `postinstall`. Several of those scripts download binaries — `cypress`, `sharp`, `@swc/core`, `@parcel/watcher`, `@tailwindcss/oxide`, `nice-napi`, `unix-dgram`. If nothing's eating CPU, one of those network-pulling postinstalls is almost certainly stalled.

Most likely culprit by a wide margin: **Cypress**. The Cypress binary is ~100MB+, the postinstall pulls it from `download.cypress.io`, and it routinely hangs behind a VPN/proxy. None of it is needed for `nx build route-planner-v2` (Cypress is e2e-only).

Suggested next step — cancel and retry skipping Cypress + getting visibility into the rest:

```bash
# in your shell
^C  # cancel current install if still running

CYPRESS_INSTALL_BINARY=0 yarn install --inline-builds
```

`--inline-builds` prints each postinstall script's output as it runs, so if a different binary fetch is the one stuck (sharp / swc / @tailwindcss/oxide), you'll see which.

If you want a quick diagnostic on what the current yarn is doing before killing it, run in another shell:

```bash
ps -ef | grep -E "cypress|node-gyp|prebuild|sharp|swc|tailwindcss" | grep -v grep
```

`unix-dgram` just finished its node-gyp compile (those warnings are harmless v8 API drift). It's in the middle of the Link step working through postinstalls. Confirmed done so far: `cypress` (skipped), `core-js` x2, `@danmarshall/deckgl-typings`, `unix-dgram`.

Still ahead, mostly silent because they're network-bound binary downloads:
- `@swc/core` — prebuilt Rust binary
- `@parcel/watcher` — prebuilt native
- `@tailwindcss/oxide` — prebuilt Rust binary
- `sharp` — prebuilt libvips binaries (largest, ~tens of MB)
- `@sentry/cli` — binary download
- `nice-napi` — another node-gyp build
- `maplibre-gl`, `nx`, `core-js-pure` — JS-only postinstalls

`sharp` + `@sentry/cli` are the slowest of these on a fresh cache.

To get visibility without killing it, in another shell:

```bash
# show any active native builds or binary downloads
ps -ef | grep -E "node-gyp|sentry-cli|swc|sharp|parcel|oxide|prebuild" | grep -v grep

# show what the yarn process is touching (network sockets included)
lsof -p $(pgrep -f "yarn install" | head -1) 2>/dev/null | grep -E "TCP|REG" | head -30
```

`bin/post-install` (no `.js`, no path prefix) is the signature of **`nx`**'s postinstall — it starts/contacts the Nx daemon and on a fresh install will try to ping Nx Cloud. Given your `nx.json` has `nxCloudAccessToken` set, the postinstall is likely waiting on an outbound HTTP call to `nx.app` that's stalling.

```bash

```

Two ways forward; the simpler one is to just kill the stuck child and let yarn move on (yarn treats a killed postinstall as failed-but-non-fatal and continues to the next package).

```bash

PID=$(pgrep -f "node ./bin/post-install" | head -1)

```

Yarn will print a warning about `nx@npm:19.6.5 couldn't be built successfully` and continue to `@parcel/watcher` / `@tailwindcss/oxide` / `sharp` / `@sentry/cli` / etc. That's fine — `nx`'s build script just sets up the daemon, which is not required for `nx build route-planner-v2`.

If yarn finishes with `nx`'s build marked failed, the install is still usable.

If you'd rather not depend on a kill-the-child trick, the alternative is to remove `nxCloudAccessToken` from `nx.json` for the duration of the install, then add it back. Tell me which you'd prefer.

### CLAUDE (2026-05-28T12:33:33.041Z)

Yarn itself is parked in `S+` with **no children and no sockets** — likely waiting on stdio pipes from the postinstall we SIGKILL'd. The pipes leaked. The kill-the-child trick wasn't clean enough for Yarn Berry. We need to kill yarn and restart with nx's postinstall preemptively skipped so it never hangs in the first place.

Two options for skipping nx's postinstall on retry — both work, pick one:

**Option A (quickest, no file edits)** — drop the Nx Cloud token from the env so nx's postinstall has nothing to dial out to:

```bash
# in yarn's terminal
kill -9 70996

# retry with nx.json's cloud token blanked at the env layer
NX_CLOUD_ACCESS_TOKEN= NX_NO_CLOUD=true NX_DAEMON=false \
NX_SKIP_NX_CACHE_INSTALL=true CYPRESS_INSTALL_BINARY=0 \
yarn install --inline-builds
```

If nx still picks the token out of `nx.json` and hangs again, fall back to B.

**Option B (definitive)** — tell yarn outright to not run nx's build script. Add this to `package.json` (anywhere at the top level):

```json
"dependenciesMeta": {
  "nx@19.6.5": { "built": false }
}
```

Then `kill -9 70996 && CYPRESS_INSTALL_BINARY=0 yarn install --inline-builds`. Yarn will skip the postinstall entirely; nx's bin still works because the daemon isn't required for `nx build`.

### CLAUDE (2026-05-28T12:36:13.940Z)

`yarn build` won't work directly — `package.json` has `"build": "nx build"` which targets `dashboard` (the workspace `defaultProject`). For route-planner-v2 you want the explicit form. Recommended:

```bash
NX_DAEMON=false NX_NO_CLOUD=true \
yarn nx build route-planner-v2
```

(`nx build route-planner-v2` works too; the `yarn` prefix just guarantees node resolution via the workspace.)

What to expect:

1. Next.js will auto-load `apps/route-planner-v2/.env.local` before evaluating `next.config.js`, so `ENV=test` will be set and `assetPrefix` will stay local.
2. Build output lands at `dist/apps/route-planner-v2/`.
3. The `NX_DAEMON/NX_NO_CLOUD` envs keep the daemon and Nx Cloud out of the build path (without them, `nx build` may try to dial the cloud and hang on the same network call we hit during install).
4. First build is slow — expect 2–5 minutes (compiles `@ncc/common`, `@ncc/ui`, etc. plus the app itself).

Once it finishes, the run-locally step (mirrors what `Dockerfile.template` does in prod):

```bash
cd dist/apps/route-planner-v2
yarn install          # installs the runtime deps listed in the emitted package.json
yarn start            # next start on :3000
```

Then open `http://localhost:3000/route-planner` (the app sets `basePath: '/route-planner'` in `next.config.js`).

Stack shows nx's native Rust module (`19.6.5-nx.darwin-arm64.node`) with idle tokio workers — the JS↔Rust IPC for the project graph is deadlocked. This is an nx internal issue, not your code.

Two paths. Try **A** first (5 second tweak); fall back to **B** if it still hangs.

**A — disable plugin isolation + clear nx cache**

```bash
# kill the whole nx subtree
pkill -9 -f "nx build route-planner-v2"
pkill -9 -f "nx/src/project-graph/plugins/isolation/plugin-worker"

# clear nx graph cache (it's been built in a deadlocked state)
rm -rf node_modules/.cache/nx .nx/cache .nx/workspace-data

# retry with all nx infra knobs off
NX_DAEMON=false NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false NX_NO_CLOUD=true \
NX_SKIP_NX_CACHE=true NX_VERBOSE_LOGGING=true \
yarn nx build route-planner-v2
```

`NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false` runs project-graph plugins in the main process, avoiding the worker-socket deadlock. `NX_VERBOSE_LOGGING=true` will print what step it's on so we can see if a different stage hangs.

**B — bypass nx entirely, run `next build` directly**

`@nx/next:build` is mostly a wrapper that copies `package.json` into `dist/` and invokes `next build`. We can do that by hand:

```bash
cd apps/route-planner-v2
yarn next build      # writes .next/ inside the app dir
```

The `.next/` output works for `next start` locally; you just lose the dist-style packaging. If you want the dist layout for parity with prod, we can write a tiny copy step after — but for "run it locally," `next start` from the app dir works.

Try A and report what verbose logging prints. If A still deadlocks, B is the escape hatch.

### CLAUDE (2026-05-28T12:52:43.036Z)

```bash
yarn next start -p 4200
```

Then open: `http://localhost:4200/route-planner`

Two notes:

- **Use port 4200**, not 3000. Your `.env.local` has `HOST=http://localhost:4200` — that's used for IAM redirect callbacks. Run on a different port and login will redirect to a dead URL.
- **`/route-planner` is required** in the URL — the app's `next.config.js` sets `basePath: '/route-planner'`, so the root path `/` won't render anything.

The server reads `.env.local` again at startup, so the prod `BFF_HOST` / `IAM_HOST` you have in there will be in effect (API calls hit `bff.nextbillion.ai`, login hits `iam.nextbillion.ai`).

This is the wall. CORS error is the BFF saying *"I don't allow `localhost:3000` as an origin."* The BFF whitelists `*.nextbillion.ai` and `*.a.run.app` (the Cloud Run preview hostnames). `localhost` isn't on the list — and we can't fix that client-side.

You can also see this in `apps/route-planner-v2/.env` (the one you just opened): `BFF_HOST=http://localhost:3000`. That's the *intended* local-dev setup — `docs/01 - dev setup.md` lays out the dependency chain `NCC → BFF → Waymor → [Tokamak, Postgres]`. The team's expectation is that you run BFF locally too. Then BFF's CORS happily accepts `localhost`.

Three realistic paths from here:

**A. Run BFF locally (matches the team's documented setup).** Clone `github.com/nextbillion/bff`, follow its README, `yarn start:dev` on port 3000, then restart ncc on a different port (the `.env` defaults assume ncc on 4200, BFF on 3000). Heaviest setup but the only path that gives you a real working app locally.

**B. Use the preview deploy infrastructure instead of running locally.** That's what the team built `yarn preview:deploy` for — same Docker image, but deployed to Cloud Run, gets a `*.a.run.app` URL the BFF allows. Quick recipe:

```bash
# from workspace root, after `gcloud auth login`
yarn preview:deploy route-planner-v2 jw-local
```

You get a public `https://console-preview-route-planner-v2-jw-local-<hash>.a.run.app/route-planner` URL with full auth + BFF working. Tears down with `yarn preview:teardown route-planner-v2 jw-local`. Details in `docs/09 - preview deployments.md`.

**C. Read-only inspection of the UI shell.** Keep the current `localhost:3000` setup; any page that makes a BFF call will error in DevTools but the framing/styling/routing is browseable. Fine for CSS work, not for anything functional.

Which is the right one depends on what you're trying to do. If it's just "see the app working without spinning up BFF/Waymor/Tokamak/DB," **B** is the path the team designed for. If you're doing backend-aware work, **A**.

### CLAUDE (2026-05-28T13:16:03.172Z)

The error is BFF talking to GCS, not BFF talking to you. Your *NCC* login (the `[EMAIL]` you tried in the browser) is unrelated — that's IAM/JWT auth.

What broke is **Google Cloud Application Default Credentials (ADC)** on your machine. The BFF process uses ADC to read its config from `gs://waymer/apikeys_stg/orgs_v2`, and ADC is currently authenticated as `[EMAIL]` — which doesn't have `storage.objects.get` on the `waymer` bucket.

`gcloud auth login` and `gcloud auth application-default login` are **two separate caches**. Even if `gcloud auth login` shows your work email, the ADC cache (which apps actually use) might still be your personal account. Confirm:

```bash
gcloud auth application-default print-access-token | head -c 50 ; echo
gcloud auth list                                       # which one is *active for gcloud CLI*
```

Then either:

**Option 1 — point ADC at your work account** (simplest if your @nextbillion.ai account has the bucket grant):

```bash
gcloud auth application-default login
# in the browser → pick [EMAIL]
# restart the BFF process so it picks up the new ADC file
```

**Option 2 — use a service-account JSON** (what `docs/01 - dev setup.md` recommends for this exact purpose):

```bash
# get the service-account JSON from a teammate (per the doc)
export GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS="/abs/path/to/sa-key.json"
# restart BFF in the same shell so it inherits the env var
```

`GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` takes precedence over the gcloud ADC cache, so Option 2 won't conflict with whatever's in `gcloud auth application-default`.

After either fix, hit `/route-planner` again — the same call should return 200 with the apikey config.

### CLAUDE (2026-05-28T13:19:38.252Z)

That's a *build-time* issue. `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` env vars are baked into the **client bundle** when `next build` runs — they're not read at startup. Your earlier build had `NEXT_PUBLIC_BFF_HOST=https://bff.nextbillion.ai` in env, so the prod URL is inlined into every client chunk. Changing it at `next start` only affects server-side fetches.

(That's exactly why your server-side calls *did* hit localhost — `BFF_HOST` is read at runtime — while client-side calls still hit prod.)

Fix: rebuild with the local BFF in env.

```bash
# stop the server (Ctrl-C)

# from apps/route-planner-v2 — REBUILD with the right NEXT_PUBLIC_* set
ENV=preview NEXT_PUBLIC_ENV=preview \
HOST=http://localhost:3001 \
BASE=/route-planner NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE=/route-planner \
BFF_HOST=http://localhost:3000 \
NEXT_PUBLIC_BFF_HOST=http://localhost:3000 \
IAM_HOST=https://iam-stg.nextbillion.ai \
IAM_CLIENT_ID=adac0e93-69ce-4f3d-936d-87867a04f0ce \
yarn next build --no-lint

# then start with the same env
ENV=preview NEXT_PUBLIC_ENV=preview \
HOST=http://localhost:3001 \
BASE=/route-planner NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE=/route-planner \
BFF_HOST=http://localhost:3000 \
NEXT_PUBLIC_BFF_HOST=http://localhost:3000 \
IAM_HOST=https://iam-stg.nextbillion.ai \
IAM_CLIENT_ID=adac0e93-69ce-4f3d-936d-87867a04f0ce \
yarn next start -p 3001
```

Heads-up: client-side calls will now go cross-origin from `http://localhost:3001` (NCC) to `http://localhost:3000` (BFF). Even though both are localhost, **different ports = different origins**, so BFF needs to send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: http://localhost:3001` (or echo the origin) with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`. Local BFFs usually have a permissive CORS config for localhost — if you get a CORS error after the rebuild, that's the next thing to check (`@nestjs/common`'s `enableCors` config in the BFF repo).

Also worth updating `apps/route-planner-v2/.env.local` to permanently reflect these values so you don't have to pass the inline env every time.

So `.env.local` overrides `.env`, and your inline command-line env overrides both. The "Environments: .env.local, .env" line is Next.js just listing which files it loaded — not announcing precedence.

Your build should be picking up `NEXT_PUBLIC_BFF_HOST=http://localhost:3000` from the shell. Let it finish, then run step 4 from earlier (`grep -l "localhost:3000" .next/static/chunks/*.js`) to confirm.

### CLAUDE (2026-05-28T14:16:25.113Z)

Before I dive in — i18n setup is a big footprint and one decision needs your sign-off:

**next-intl needs a new dep + a next.config.js wrap.** The dep add (`next-intl@^3`) means another `yarn install` for you (so we'll need to remember the `--inline-builds` flags + the nx-postinstall workaround). The config change wraps `next.config.js` with `createNextIntlPlugin` *outside* the existing `withSentryConfig`/`withNx` chain. Both are reversible but non-trivial.

Also, "all visible strings in route-planner-v2" is realistically a multi-day effort — there are hundreds of files. My plan:

1. **Wire the framework end-to-end** (next-intl plugin, request config, `NextIntlClientProvider` in layout, header globe-icon switcher persisting to a `NEXT_LOCALE` cookie). EN/PT-BR/ES-MX catalogs exist with the keys I can mechanically lift in this session.
2. **Translate a meaningful starter set** — input toolbar, creating-routes dialog, save-data dialog, preferences panels (the high-traffic surfaces I've already seen in lint output).
3. **Leave a follow-up TODO** for the rest of the screens with a grep pattern to find them. PT-BR / ES-MX values get my best-effort translations, all flagged with `// TODO: native review` in the catalog files.

Two checkpoints I want from you before kicking off:

 "content": "import {cookies} from 'next/headers'\nimport {getRequestConfig} from 'next-intl/server'\n\nexport const SUPPORTED_LOCALES = ['en', 'pt-BR', 'es-MX'] as const\nexport type Locale = (typeof SUPPORTED_LOCALES)[number]\nexport const DEFAULT_LOCALE: Locale = 'en'\nexport const LOCALE_COOKIE = 'NEXT_LOCALE'\n\nfunction isSupported(value: string | undefined): value is Locale {\n  return !!value && (SUPPORTED_LOCALES as readonly string[]).includes(value)\n}\n\nexport default getRequestConfig(async () => {\n  const cookieValue = cookies().get(LOCALE_COOKIE)?.value\n  const locale: Locale = isSupported(cookieValue) ? cookieValue : DEFAULT_LOCALE\n\n  return {\n    locale,\n    messages: (await import(`../messages/${locale}.json`)).default,\n  }\n})\n"
}
```

 "content": "'use client'\nimport {useState} from 'react'\nimport IconButton from '@mui/material/IconButton'\nimport Menu from '@mui/material/Menu'\nimport MenuItem from '@mui/material/MenuItem'\nimport LanguageIcon from '@mui/icons-material/Language'\nimport {useLocale, useTranslations} from 'next-intl'\n\nconst LOCALES = ['en', 'pt-BR', 'es-MX'] as const\n\nexport function LocaleSwitcher() {\n  const locale = useLocale()\n  const t = useTranslations('locales')\n  const [anchor, setAnchor] = useState<HTMLElement | null>(null)\n\n  const select = (next: (typeof LOCALES)[number]) => {\n    document.cookie = `NEXT_LOCALE=${next}; path=/; max-age=31536000; SameSite=Lax`\n    setAnchor(null)\n    window.location.reload()\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <>\n      <IconButton\n        size=\"small\"\n        onClick={(e) => setAnchor(e.currentTarget)}\n        sx={{\n          position: 'fixed',\n          top: 8,\n          right: 16,\n          zIndex: (theme) => theme.zIndex.drawer + 2,\n        }}\n        aria-label=\"change language\"\n      >\n        <LanguageIcon />\n      </IconButton>\n      <Menu\n        anchorEl={anchor}\n        open={Boolean(anchor)}\n        onClose={() => setAnchor(null)}\n      >\n        {LOCALES.map((loc) => (\n          <MenuItem\n            key={loc}\n            selected={loc === locale}\n            onClick={() => select(loc)}\n          >\n            {t(loc)}\n          </MenuItem>\n        ))}\n      </Menu>\n    </>\n  )\n}\n"
}

Summary of i18n changes:

- `package.json`: added `"next-intl": "^3.26.0"` — **needs `yarn install` again** (same workaround as before).
- `apps/route-planner-v2/i18n/request.ts`: server config — reads `NEXT_LOCALE` cookie, loads matching JSON.

- `apps/route-planner-v2/next.config.js`: wrapped outermost with `createNextIntlPlugin('./i18n/request.ts')`.

- `apps/route-planner-v2/app/layout.tsx`: async, reads `getLocale()` + `getMessages()`, wraps with `NextIntlClientProvider`, renders `<LocaleSwitcher />`.
- `apps/route-planner-v2/components/locale-switcher.tsx`: floating globe-icon button (top-right, fixed position). Opens MUI Menu, writes `NEXT_LOCALE` cookie, reloads.

Two issues in those logs:

1. **Port mismatch**: you started dev on 3001, but `HOST=http://localhost:4200` — that doesn't match BFF's CORS allowlist for 3001, and IAM redirect URIs are now wrong relative to the running port. Most likely cause of the 404 chain.

2. The BFF `organizations.get` 500 is unrelated to the 404 — it's caught and logged, layout continues.

Run on 4200 so everything aligns (BFF allows it, HOST matches, IAM callback returns to the right port):

```bash
# stop the 3001 dev server (Ctrl-C), then:
ENV=preview NEXT_PUBLIC_ENV=preview \
HOST=http://localhost:4200 BASE=/route-planner NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE=/route-planner \
BFF_HOST=http://localhost:3000 NEXT_PUBLIC_BFF_HOST=http://localhost:3000 \
IAM_HOST=https://iam-stg.nextbillion.ai \
IAM_CLIENT_ID=adac0e93-69ce-4f3d-936d-87867a04f0ce \
yarn next dev -p 4200
```

Open `http://localhost:4200/route-planner` (note: with the basePath, the URL bar will end up redirecting through `/` first — that's fine).

If you're still on port 3001 by preference, instead set `HOST=http://localhost:3001` and tell me — we'll also need to add `http://localhost:3001` to your BFF's CORS allowlist (one line in `/Users/[USER]/workspace/bff/src/main.ts`).

Also — did `yarn install` complete successfully with the new `next-intl` dep? The dev server appears to have compiled successfully which is a good sign, but worth confirming. If you see any module-not-found error mentioning `next-intl` in the dev console, the install needs a re-run.

### CLAUDE (2026-05-28T15:02:22.944Z)

I have a complete picture. Here's what's going on:

**Existing infrastructure (good news — lots of it):**

- Profiles are already named via `preferences.fileName` (the "Configuration Name" field). Default name is `'Default'`.
- BFF already has two storage buckets: `dir: 'preference'` (preferences JSON) and `dir: 'input'` (input-data JSON), both keyed by `fileName`. Calls go through `/config/save` and `/config/get`.
- Save actions exist: `savePreferenceConfiguration` and `saveInputSet` (in `models/input/input-core.ts`).
- Load actions exist: `loadPreferenceConfiguration` and `loadInputConfiguration`. `loadPreferenceList` even auto-loads the "last" used profile on init.

**The gap (one specific block of code):**

`saveInputSet` in `models/input/input-core.ts:1288-1329` **intentionally strips `rawData.rows` for jobs and shipments**, but persists them in full for vehicles and depots:

```js
// jobs (and shipments — same pattern)
inputData['job'] = {
  rawData: { header: [], rows: [], attachedRows: [] },  // ← stripped
  mapConfig: rootState.inputCore.job.mapConfig,         // ← saved
  dataMapMenuList: rootState.inputCore.job.dataMapMenuList, // ← saved
}
// vehicles (and depots — saved whole)
inputData['vehicle'] = rootState.inputCore.vehicle        // ← full
```

So **mappings already persist per profile** — that half of your ask is already done. The missing half is the jobs/shipments rows themselves.

`loadInputConfiguration` (lines 1250-1287) calls `setInputSet('job', inputData.job)` — meaning if the payload contains `rawData.rows`, they'll be restored. So the load path needs no changes; only the save path.

**Why the asymmetry probably exists:** vehicles/depots are typically dozens of rows; jobs/shipments can be thousands. Saving thousands of rows to a GCS-backed `/config/save` could hit size limits or be slow.

**The fix (small, ~10 lines):** Remove the strip in `saveInputSet` so jobs/shipments persist their rows just like vehicles/depots do.

Before I make the change, two design choices:

### CLAUDE (2026-05-28T15:03:43.170Z)

**Task 5 done.** Single-spot fix in `apps/route-planner-v2/models/input/input-core.ts` (the `saveInputSet` effect): jobs and shipments now persist their `rawData` (header + rows + attachedRows) alongside `mapConfig` + `dataMapMenuList`, matching the existing vehicle/depot behavior.

Net effect:

- **Save** (`Save data` action / save-data-dialog): the full uploaded job/shipment grid is bundled into the profile's `/config/save` payload under `dir=input` with the profile's `fileName`.
- **Load** (existing `loadInputConfiguration`): `setInputSet('job', inputData.job)` spreads the saved `rawData` over state, so rows + mappings re-appear in the data-mapper. No changes needed on the load side.
- **Unsaved-changes detection** (`computeSavedStateSnapshot` + `hasUnsavedChanges` in `(input)/page.tsx`): already snapshots `jobRows`/`shipmentRows`. Was correctly aware of these all along; what was missing was the ability to actually persist them. Now the snapshot will line up with what's saved.

Verification path:
1. Load a profile or start fresh.
2. Upload some jobs (and/or shipments). Map columns.
3. Hit Save (or "Save data" in the dialog).
4. Reload the page or switch profiles and back.
5. Jobs/shipments rows + mappings come back.

No HMR concerns — Rematch effects rebuild on save; just reload the page in dev.

### CLAUDE (2026-05-28T15:29:30.671Z)

Done. Two-line behavior change:

- `utils/parser/col-parsers.ts:859` — `';'` → `'|'`.
- `hooks/input/use-current-input.ts:141-149` — added `MULTI_SELECT_ALLOWED = new Set(['description'])`; `getDisabledList` strips those values from its lockout list so the dropdown stays open for repeat selection on other columns.

How it flows end-to-end now:

1. User clicks **Description** on column A — `dataMappings` gains `{index: A, value: 'description'}`.
2. User clicks the dropdown on column B — Description is **no longer disabled** (because of the exemption). User picks it.
3. `dataMappings` now has two `{value: 'description'}` entries.
4. At parse time (`data-parser.ts:154-158`), `descNum` counts the description mappings and sets `iMultiDesc = descNum > 1`. When true, `parseDescription` concatenates: `target.description = 'A_value|B_value'`.

Caveats / things to know:

- **Ordering**: concatenation follows iteration order of `dataMappings`, which is insertion order. If the user picks Description on column 5 before column 2, the resulting string is `col5|col2`. If you'd like strict column-index ordering, that's a small follow-up tweak in the data-parser. Let me know.
- Applies to all four entity types (jobs, shipments, vehicles, depots) — they all share this parser path and all use the literal `'description'` map key.
- Existing single-column Description behavior is unchanged (`descNum === 1` → `target[key] = value`, no separator).
- `removeDataMapConfig` still removes one column-mapping at a time via index, so users can de-select individual columns from the description set.

Save propagates via HMR.

### CLAUDE (2026-05-28T15:55:31.543Z)

All five red-box sections wired. Save propagates via HMR.

Summary of the catalog additions (translations applied to en/pt-BR/es-MX):

- `depots` — "Use Depots" → "Usar depósitos" / "Usar almacenes"; description; "Add depots to this route plan" → "Adicionar depósitos a este plano de rotas" / "Agregar almacenes a este plan de rutas".
- `routing` — title, description, mode toggle (Truck/Car → Caminhão/Carro / Camión/Auto), Traffic timestamp, Avoid/Exclude descriptions + tooltips + placeholders, Select All, all 9 road-type menu items (Toll, Highway, Ferry, Left/Right/Sharp Turn, U-Turn, Service Road, None), Truck mode fields, Hazmat label/desc.
- `routeDescription` — title, description, placeholder.
- `timezone` — title, description, "Select Timezone", search placeholder, ISO option label + subtext.
- `connection` — "Send Route To", description, "Select", "None".

The trick for the **menu items inside Avoid/Exclude dropdowns**: refactored `createPreferencesSelect` so the inner component calls `useTranslations('routing')` itself and translates each option value via a key prefix (e.g. `road_${value}` → `road_toll` / `road_left_turn`). The static `AVOID_OPTIONS` / `EXCLUDE_OPTIONS` / `HAZMAT_OPTIONS` shared files stay untouched (English labels remain as the fallback). Search inside the dropdown also uses the localized labels — `filterOptions` is now built inside the component using the localized `labelFor()`.

Hazmat material names (Explosives, Gas, etc.) get the same prefix-based translation path (`hazmat_explosives`, `hazmat_gas`, ...) — those catalog keys aren't populated yet so the component will fall back to the English `label` via the try/catch on `t()`. Add `hazmat_*` entries when you want those translated (Hazmat fields only appear when Truck mode is active, which is why they weren't in the red box).

Reload the page after switching locale (the LocaleSwitcher does this) and the red-boxed sections should be fully translated.

### CLAUDE (2026-05-28T16:01:55.757Z)

Done. **Light is now the default** for fresh sessions; TomTom Dark stays in the selector at position 5 so you can still pick it.

One thing to know: the `MapStyleSelector` persists the user's last pick in localStorage (`map-style` key, scoped per `storageScope`). If you had switched to TomTom Dark previously, your browser will still restore it on load. To force the new default, either:

- Pick "Light" once in the selector, or
- Clear localStorage in DevTools (Application → Local Storage → delete the `map-style` key)

HMR will pick up the change immediately.

 "new_string": "import {useMemo, useState} from 'react'\nimport {useTranslations} from 'next-intl'\nimport {\n  MenuGroup,\n  MenuInfo,\n  MetaMapOption,\n  getGroupDisplayOrder,\n  groupAndSortMenuItems,\n} from './mapping-config/options/interface'\n\nimport InfoOutlined from '@mui/icons-material/InfoOutlined'\nimport {Popover} from '@mui/material'\nimport {Tooltip} from '@ncc/ui'\nimport {InputType} from '../../../models/input/input-core'\n\n// Translation key for a MenuInfo value. Sanitizes characters that next-intl\n// would interpret as nested-key delimiters (dots) and characters that aren't\n// valid in catalog keys (#, spaces).\nfunction toFieldKey(value: string): string {\n  return value.replace(/#/g, '_').replace(/\\./g, '__').replace(/\\s+/g, '_')\n}\n\n// Resolve a localized label for a menu item, falling back to the static\n// English `label` on the option (or its value) when no catalog entry exists.\nfunction useFieldLabel() {\n  const t = useTranslations('mapperFields')\n  return (option: MenuInfo): string => {\n    const key = toFieldKey(option.value)\n    try {\n      const translated = t(key)\n      if (translated && translated !== key) return translated\n    } catch {\n      /* fall through */\n    }\n    return option.label ?? option.value\n  }\n}\n\nfunction useGroupLabel() {\n  const t = useTranslations('mapperGroups')\n  return (group: MenuGroup | string): string => {\n    try {\n      const translated = t(group as string)\n      if (translated && translated !== group) return translated\n    } catch {\n      /* fall through */\n    }\n    return group as string\n  }\n}"
}

### CLAUDE (2026-05-28T16:13:24.273Z)

Done. HMR will pick it up — switch to PT-BR via the globe icon and reload.

What's now translated:

**Header / chrome (page-level):**
- "Map your data fields with NB fields" → "Mapeie seus campos de dados com os campos NB"
- "AI Mapping" → "Mapeamento por IA"
- "Reset Mapping" → "Redefinir mapeamento"

**Action bar buttons:**
- "Add attribute" → "Adicionar atributo"
- "Edit" / "Delete" / "Save" / "Cancel"
- AI Mapping loading message

**Mapping popover:**
- Group headers via `mapperGroups.*` (General → Geral, Time → Tempo, Financials → Financeiro, Location info → Informações de localização, Skill & Capacities → Habilidades e capacidades, Driver Regulations → Regulamentos do motorista, etc.).
- "Dispatch Metadata" → "Metadados de despacho" (used for both the label + button).
- Top-level field items via `mapperFields.*` (ID, Description, Priority, Setup, Sequence Order, Start Time, End Time, Service Time, Pickup/Skills/Delivery Capacities, Revenue, Outsourcing Cost, Depot IDs, Location, Address).
- "Add" submenu button.

**How field translation works:**

Added two helpers at the top of `mapping-popover.tsx`:

- `useFieldLabel()` — derives a sanitized key from `option.value` (strips `#`, `.`, spaces), looks it up in `mapperFields`, falls back to `option.label` if no catalog entry exists. So if you upload a profile that has a unique field type you haven't translated, the English label still renders.
- `useGroupLabel()` — same pattern for `MenuGroup` enum values, keyed by their literal English string (e.g. `'General'`, `'Skill & Capacities'`).

**Explicitly left in English** (scope guard — these are large surfaces with hundreds of numbered children):

- Submenu children (Skill 1–6, Capacity 1–6, Depot ID 1–5, Start Time 1–10, etc.). Translate by adding entries to `mapperFields` using the sanitized value pattern. Example: `'skill 1'` → key `skill_1` → add to catalog.
- Vehicle-specific advanced fields (Break/Layover/Cost & Constraints) — same pattern, just more keys to add.
- The `MetaMap` connection-specific options (Samsara/Motive/Geotab/etc.) — those come from `metaOptionList` which the popover passes through unchanged; same `fieldLabel` helper could be reused if you want them translated.

Add to `mapperFields` whenever you spot an English label that should be translated — no code change required, just a catalog entry per value.

 "content": "'use client'\nimport {useState} from 'react'\nimport {Box, Button, TextField} from '@mui/material'\nimport FilterAltOutlined from '@mui/icons-material/FilterAltOutlined'\nimport {DateTimePicker} from '@mui/x-date-pickers'\nimport {AdapterDayjs} from '@mui/x-date-pickers/AdapterDayjs'\nimport {LocalizationProvider} from '@mui/x-date-pickers/LocalizationProvider'\nimport dayjs, {Dayjs} from 'dayjs'\nimport {useTranslations} from 'next-intl'\nimport {useDispatch, useSelector} from 'react-redux'\nimport {Dispatch, RootState} from '../../../models/input/store'\nimport {TIME_FORMAT} from '../../../shared/const'\n\n// Convert a wildcard pattern (`*` = any sequence) into an anchored,\n// case-insensitive RegExp. Returns `null` (= match-anything) when the\n// pattern is empty so callers can short-circuit without building a regex.\nfunction wildcardMatch(pattern: string, value: string): boolean {\n  if (!pattern.trim()) return true\n  const escaped = pattern\n    .replace(/[.+?^${}()|[\\]\\\\]/g, '\\\\$&')\n    .replace(/\\*/g, '.*')\n  return new RegExp(`^${escaped}$`, 'i').test(value ?? '')\n}\n\nexport function JobFilterBar() {\n  const t = useTranslations('jobFilter')\n  const dispatch = useDispatch<Dispatch>()\n  const jobs = useSelector(\n    (state: RootState) => state.inputCore.output.job ?? [],\n  )\n  const timezone = useSelector(\n    (state: RootState) => state.inputCore.preferences.timezone,\n  )\n\n  const [idPattern, setIdPattern] = useState('')\n  const [descPattern, setDescPattern] = useState('')\n  const [twStart, setTwStart] = useState<Dayjs | null>(null)\n  const [twEnd, setTwEnd] = useState<Dayjs | null>(null)\n\n  const apply = () => {\n    const startUnix = twStart ? twStart.unix() : null\n    const endUnix = twEnd ? twEnd.unix() : null\n    const timeFilterActive = startUnix !== null || endUnix !== null\n\n    const matching: number[] = []\n    jobs.forEach((job: any, index: number) => {\n      if (!wildcardMatch(idPattern, String(job.id ?? ''))) return\n      if (!wildcardMatch(descPattern, String(job.description ?? ''))) return\n      if (timeFilterActive) {\n        const tws = (job.time_windows ?? []) as [number, number][]\n        if (tws.length === 0) return // jobs without windows can't satisfy a time filter\n        const anyOverlap = tws.some(([s, e]) => {\n          const startOk = startUnix === null || e >= startUnix\n          const endOk = endUnix === null || s <= endUnix\n          return startOk && endOk\n        })\n        if (!anyOverlap) return\n      }\n      matching.push(index)\n    })\n    dispatch.inputPreview.setSelectedJobs(matching)\n  }\n\n  const clear = () => {\n    setIdPattern('')\n    setDescPattern('')\n    setTwStart(null)\n    setTwEnd(null)\n    dispatch.inputPreview.setSelectedJobs(jobs.map((_, i) => i))\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <Box\n      sx={{\n        display: 'flex',\n        gap: 1,\n        alignItems: 'center',\n        flexWrap: 'wrap',\n        mb: 1.5,\n        p: 1.5,\n        bgcolor: 'rgba(244, 244, 247, 1)',\n        borderRadius: 1,\n      }}\n    >\n      <FilterAltOutlined sx={{color: 'text.secondary'}} />\n      <TextField\n        size=\"small\"\n        label={t('idLabel')}\n        placeholder={t('idPlaceholder')}\n        value={idPattern}\n        onChange={(e) => setIdPattern(e.target.value)}\n        sx={{width: 180}}\n      />\n      <TextField\n        size=\"small\"\n        label={t('descriptionLabel')}\n        placeholder={t('descriptionPlaceholder')}\n        value={descPattern}\n        onChange={(e) => setDescPattern(e.target.value)}\n        sx={{width: 240}}\n      />\n      <LocalizationProvider dateAdapter={AdapterDayjs}>\n        <DateTimePicker\n          label={t('twStartLabel')}\n          value={twStart}\n          onChange={setTwStart}\n          format={TIME_FORMAT}\n          timezone={\n            timezone === 'iso' ? undefined : timezone || undefined\n          }\n          slotProps={{textField: {size: 'small', sx: {width: 220}}}}\n        />\n        <DateTimePicker\n          label={t('twEndLabel')}\n          value={twEnd}\n          onChange={setTwEnd}\n          format={TIME_FORMAT}\n          timezone={\n            timezone === 'iso' ? undefined : timezone || undefined\n          }\n          slotProps={{textField: {size: 'small', sx: {width: 220}}}}\n        />\n      </LocalizationProvider>\n      <Button variant=\"contained\" size=\"small\" onClick={apply}>\n        {t('apply')}\n      </Button>\n      <Button variant=\"text\" size=\"small\" onClick={clear}>\n        {t('clear')}\n      </Button>\n    </Box>\n  )\n}\n"
}

### CLAUDE (2026-05-28T16:29:12.562Z)

**Direct answers to your two questions:**

1. **Yes, the pickers DO use `preferences.timezone`** — `JobFilterBar` reads `state.inputCore.preferences.timezone` and passes it as the `timezone` prop to both `<DateTimePicker>` instances. So if your prefs say `America/Sao_Paulo`, typing `12:00` in the picker means 12:00 in São Paulo, and `.unix()` returns the UTC seconds for that moment — which is the same scale `time_windows` is stored in (confirmed: `col-parsers.ts:927` returns `Math.round(value.getTime() / 1000)` after parsing in the prefs timezone).

2. **24-hour clock + locale-aware format are now in:** `ampm={false}` forces 24h on both pickers, and `<LocalizationProvider adapterLocale={dayjsLocale}>` switches dayjs's locale to match next-intl (so PT-BR users get DD/MM/YYYY, etc.). Eager imports of `dayjs/locale/{en,pt-br,es-mx}` at the top of the file ensure the locales are registered before the picker mounts.

**On "filter not working" — I added a diagnostic.** When you click **Aplicar filtro**, open the browser DevTools console — you'll see a `[JobFilterBar] apply` line with:

- `total` — how many jobs are in `output.job`
- `matching` — how many were selected
- `timeFilterRejections` — how many failed the overlap test (had time windows but none overlapped)
- `noTimeWindows` — how many were skipped because they had no `time_windows` at all
- `startUnix` / `endUnix` — the unix seconds the pickers produced
- `sampleJobTws` — the first job's `time_windows` array, so we can eyeball the units

Paste that console line back to me. Given the screenshot shows visible jobs all *should* overlap 12:00–13:00, one of these is almost certainly true:

- The pickers are emitting a unix value in the wrong timezone (would explain unexpected `timeFilterRejections`).
- The selected-checkbox UI updated correctly but the table still shows all rows (by design — filter only controls selection, not visibility) and you expected the visible rows to filter.
- `time_windows` on some jobs is stored differently than the array-of-`[start,end]` shape my code assumes.

The console line will pin it down in one click.

**Row highlighting** — `apps/route-planner-v2/components/input/input-preview-page/preview-table.tsx`: each cell in a selected row gets `backgroundColor: rgba(30, 85, 222, 0.08)` (a subtle blue tint matching the app's primary palette). **Tab badges → selection count** — `apps/route-planner-v2/components/input/input-preview-page/preview.tsx`: each tab now has both `count` (currently-selected) and `total` (entity count). The chip on the tab shows `count`. The visibility filter switched from `count > 0` to `total > 0` so a tab stays visible even when you've deselected everything — otherwise filtering to zero matches would hide the tab and the user couldn't reverse out.

Behavior notes:

- **Initial state**: all rows start selected by default, so badges show the same number you used to see (the total).
- **After Apply filter on Jobs**: badge drops to the number of matches. Other tabs unaffected (each entity has its own selection state).
- **Deselect everything**: badge shows `0`; tab still visible because rows exist.
- **Preferences tab**: `count` is just `countPreferences(preferences)` — same behavior as before, no selection concept there.

Want the badge to show `selected / total` instead of just `selected` (gives both numbers at a glance)? Say the word — one-line change to the `<Box>` that renders the chip.

### CLAUDE (2026-05-28T16:51:18.820Z)

Both shipped. HMR will pick them up.

**Lasso (Task #12)** — three pieces in `apps/route-planner-v2/components/input/preview-map/preview-lasso.tsx`:

- `PreviewLassoButton` — toggle in the top-left of the map area (under the existing layer-style chip), shows the lasso icon when idle and an X when active or a polygon is already drawn.
- `PreviewLassoDrawing` — mounted inside `<Map>`; activates a transparent capture div over the map while in lasso mode. Click to place vertices, double-click or click within 12px of the first vertex to close. Esc cancels. Wheel events forward to the map canvas so zoom still works mid-draw. Map drag is disabled while drawing.
- `PreviewLassoPolygon` — renders the persistent polygon (dashed blue) after close; cleared when the toggle is clicked again.

**Selection wiring** in `preview-map.tsx`:

- On close, reads `state.inputPreview.tab` and dispatches `setSelectedJobs` / `setSelectedShipments` / `setSelectedVehicles` / `setSelectedDepots` accordingly.
- Match rules:
  - **Jobs / Depots** — item matches if its `location` is inside the polygon.
  - **Shipments** — pickup OR delivery in polygon.
  - **Vehicles** — start_location OR end_location in polygon.
- Locations parsed from `"lat,lng"` string via the helper that mirrors `getLocation` in `use-input-map-layers.ts`.
- Hover tooltip is suppressed while in lasso mode so the polygon-draw cursor isn't competing with it.

**Globe move (Task #13)** — `LocaleSwitcher` is no longer fixed-position floating over the NbAppBar. It now sits inline in `page-head.tsx`'s right-aligned `<Stack>`, immediately after the **Dev Mode** toggle and before the AppsIcon menu. Spacing comes from the parent Stack's `spacing={2}` — no manual offsets.

i18n keys added for the lasso tooltip (`previewLasso.open` / `previewLasso.close` / `previewLasso.hint`) in EN/PT-BR/ES-MX.

Try it:
1. On Input Preview, switch to the Jobs tab.
2. Click the lasso button (top-left of map area).
3. Click around to define a polygon, double-click or close-near-first to finalize.
4. Selected jobs in the table should update to match.
5. Click the lasso button again to clear the polygon and exit selection mode.

### CLAUDE (2026-05-28T16:53:45.191Z)

The issue: `<DeckGL>` wraps the `<Map>` in preview-map (it doesn't in the v3 lasso's `<BaseMap>`). DeckGL's canvas overlays the Map and steals clicks, so my capture div — rendered inside `<Map>` — is below DeckGL's canvas in the stacking order.

Two fixes:

1. Move the capture div to be a **sibling of DeckGL** in `styles.root`, at high z-index, so it sits above DeckGL's canvas.
2. Keep the polygon Source/Layer and the vertex Markers inside `<Map>` (they need the Map context to render into mapbox's layer manager).

### CLAUDE (2026-05-28T16:55:21.661Z)

Fixed. HMR picks up on save.

**What changed:**

- Split the lasso into two cooperating components sharing state via a `useLassoDraft` hook:
  - `PreviewLassoDrawing` — the click-capture div. Now rendered as a **sibling of `<DeckGL>`** at `z-index: 1000`. This lifts it above DeckGL's canvas in the stacking order so clicks reach it first instead of being eaten by DeckGL's picker.
  - `PreviewLassoDraftOverlay` — the dashed polygon Source/Layer + vertex Markers. Stays **inside `<Map>`** since `Source`/`Layer`/`Marker` need the mapbox Map context to render.

- `useLassoDraft(active)` holds the shared draft state (vertices, cursor position, near-first-vertex flag) and exposes setters/resetters to both halves.

Try again:
1. Click the lasso button (left-side of map).
2. Click on the map — first vertex appears as a white-bordered blue dot.
3. Click again to add more vertices, with the dashed polygon updating live as you move the cursor.
4. Double-click anywhere or click within ~12px of your first vertex to close.
5. Items inside get selected on the active tab.

If clicks still don't land, the next layer to check is whether DeckGL is doing something weird with `controller` config — but z-index 1000 above DeckGL's canvas should be conclusive.

Found the bug. The parser stores `job.location` as `"lng,lat"` string (see `parseLocationLatLng`: it splits, **reverses**, and joins — so a "Lat,Lng" input ends up as `"lng,lat"`). My `parseLngLat` helper assumed `"lat,lng"` input and destructured it as such, then returned `[lng, lat]` — which actually swapped the two values, sending bogus coordinates to turf.

Fixing it now:

### CLAUDE (2026-05-28T16:59:19.613Z)

Fix shipped. HMR will pick it up.

**What was wrong:**

The parser canonicalizes every job/shipment/vehicle location into a `"lng,lat"` string regardless of which mapping the user picked. Concretely, `parseLocationLatLng` (col-parsers.ts:629-630) splits the user input, **calls `.reverse()`**, and joins it back — turning "Lat,Lng" into "lng,lat". `parseLocationLngLat` just keeps "lng,lat". The lat/lng-as-separate-columns path goes through `parseLocationLat`/`parseLocationLng` which appends in lng-first order when `locationStyle !== 'latlng'`.

My `parseLngLat` was named correctly but read `[lat, lng] = parts` and returned `[lng, lat]` — which silently swapped the two values for the canonical format. The polygon was drawn around São Paulo, but the points I tested were effectively `[lat_value, lng_value]` — landing in the Atlantic Ocean. Zero matches.

The fix: trust the stored canonical format and return `parts` as `[lng, lat]` directly. Now turf gets `[lng, lat]` which is exactly what `booleanPointInPolygon` expects.

[])]\n      arr[index] = item\n      return {...state, output: {...state.output, [type]: arr}}\n    },\n    setRawCell(\n      state,\n      payload: {\n        type: InputType\n        rowIndex: number\n        colIndex: number\n        value: string\n      },\n    ) {\n      const {type, rowIndex, colIndex, value} = payload\n      const inputSet = state[type]\n      const rowsLen = inputSet.rawData.rows[rowIndex]?.length ?? 0\n      const newRows = inputSet.rawData.rows.map((r) => [...r])\n      const newAttachedRows = inputSet.rawData.attachedRows.map((r) => [...r])\n      if (colIndex < rowsLen) {\n        newRows[rowIndex][colIndex] = value\n      } else {\n        const attachedColIndex = colIndex - rowsLen\n        if (!newAttachedRows[rowIndex]) {\n          newAttachedRows[rowIndex] = []\n        }\n        newAttachedRows[rowIndex][attachedColIndex] = value\n      }\n      return {\n        ...state,\n        [type]: {\n          ...inputSet,\n          rawData: {\n            ...inputSet.rawData,\n            rows: newRows,\n            attachedRows: newAttachedRows,\n          },\n        },\n      }\n    },"

 "old_string": "    async deleteData(\n      payload: {type: InputType; indexes: number[]},\n      rootState: RootState,\n    ) {",
 "new_string": "    /**\n     * Apply user-edited cell values to a single preview row.\n     *\n     * Writes overrides to BOTH halves of the model:\n     *  - `rawData.rows[rowIndex][colIndex]` (so the override survives\n     *    re-mapping / re-parse and is included when the profile is saved\n     *    via `saveInputSet`)\n     *  - `output[type][rowIndex]` (so the preview reflects the change\n     *    immediately without waiting for a full `generateOutput` pass)\n     *\n     * The row is re-parsed using the same parser the initial load uses, so\n     * derived structures like `time_windows` arrays and capacity arrays are\n     * rebuilt correctly from the new raw cell values.\n     */\n    async updatePreviewRow(\n      payload: {\n        type: InputType\n        rowIndex: number\n        columnUpdates: Record<number, string>\n      },\n      rootState: RootState,\n    ) {\n      const {type, rowIndex, columnUpdates} = payload\n      const state = rootState.inputCore\n      const inputSet = state[type]\n\n      // 1) Persist raw-cell edits so the override is part of the saved\n      //    profile and any future re-parse uses the new values.\n      for (const [colIndexStr, value] of Object.entries(columnUpdates)) {\n        dispatch.inputCore.setRawCell({\n          type,\n          rowIndex,\n          colIndex: Number(colIndexStr),\n          value,\n        })\n      }\n\n      // 2) Compute the full row WITH the overrides applied locally — we\n      //    don't read state back after the reducer dispatches above\n      //    because rematch effects don't refresh `rootState` mid-effect.\n      const baseRow = (inputSet.rawData.rows[rowIndex] ?? []).concat(\n        inputSet.rawData.attachedRows[rowIndex] ?? [],\n      )\n      const updatedRow = [...baseRow]\n      for (const [colIndexStr, value] of Object.entries(columnUpdates)) {\n        updatedRow[Number(colIndexStr)] = value\n      }\n\n      // 3) Re-parse just this row via the same entry point used at load.\n      const extConfig = {\n        timezone: state.preferences.timezone,\n      } as extraConfig\n      const connection = state.preferences.connection\n      let parsed: any\n      if (type === 'vehicle') {\n        parsed = parseVehicle(\n          // @ts-expect-error - connection type mismatch (mirrors generateOutput)\n          connection,\n          updatedRow,\n          inputSet.mapConfig.dataMappings,\n          inputSet.mapConfig.metaMappings,\n          extConfig,\n        )\n      } else if (type === 'job') {\n        parsed = parseJob(\n          // @ts-expect-error - connection type mismatch\n          connection,\n          updatedRow,\n          inputSet.mapConfig.dataMappings,\n          inputSet.mapConfig.metaMappings,\n          extConfig,\n        )\n      } else if (type === 'shipment') {\n        parsed = parseShipment(\n          // @ts-expect-error - connection type mismatch\n          connection,\n          updatedRow,\n          inputSet.mapConfig.dataMappings,\n          inputSet.mapConfig.metaMappings,\n          extConfig,\n        )\n        if (parsed) delete parsed['metadata']\n      } else if (type === 'depot') {\n        parsed = parseDepots(\n          // @ts-expect-error - connection type mismatch\n          connection,\n          updatedRow,\n          inputSet.mapConfig.dataMappings,\n          inputSet.mapConfig.metaMappings,\n          extConfig,\n        )\n      }\n\n      if (parsed) {\n        dispatch.inputCore.setOutputItem({type, index: rowIndex, item: parsed})\n      }\n    },\n    async deleteData(\n      payload: {type: InputType; indexes: number[]},\n      rootState: RootState,\n    ) {"
}

[]\n  // Stable join key for the rawRow useMemo so we don't re-init on every\n  // state-update — useMemo runs only when the underlying row changes.\n  const rawRow = useMemo(() => {\n    if (!inputSet || rowIndex == null) return [] as string[]\n    const r = inputSet.rawData.rows[rowIndex] ?? []\n    const a = inputSet.rawData.attachedRows[rowIndex] ?? []\n    return r.concat(a)\n  }, [inputSet, rowIndex])\n\n  const [values, setValues] = useState<Record<number, string>>({})\n\n  // Snapshot rawRow values into the form when the dialog opens for a\n  // (type, rowIndex) pair. Editing a different row reseeds via this same\n  // effect.\n  useEffect(() => {\n    if (!open || rowIndex == null) return\n    const initial: Record<number, string> = {}\n    for (const m of dataMappings) {\n      initial[m.index] = rawRow[m.index] ?? ''\n    }\n    setValues(initial)\n  }, [open, rowIndex, type])\n\n  const labelFor = (mappingValue: string, fallback?: string): string => {\n    const key = toFieldKey(mappingValue)\n    try {\n      const translated = fieldsT(key)\n      if (translated && translated !== key) return translated\n    } catch {\n      /* fall through */\n    }\n    return fallback ?? mappingValue\n  }\n\n  const handleSave = () => {\n    if (!type || rowIndex == null) return\n    const updates: Record<number, string> = {}\n    for (const m of dataMappings) {\n      const current = rawRow[m.index] ?? ''\n      const next = values[m.index] ?? ''\n      if (next !== current) {\n        updates[m.index] = next\n      }\n    }\n    if (Object.keys(updates).length > 0) {\n      dispatch.inputCore.updatePreviewRow({\n        type,\n        rowIndex,\n        columnUpdates: updates,\n      })\n    }\n    onClose()\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <Dialog open={open} onClose={onClose} maxWidth=\"md\" fullWidth>\n      <DialogTitle>{t('title')}</DialogTitle>\n      <DialogContent dividers>\n        <Typography variant=\"body2\" color=\"text.secondary\" sx={{mb: 2}}>\n          {t('subtitle')}\n        </Typography>\n        {dataMappings.length === 0 && (\n          <Typography variant=\"body2\" color=\"text.secondary\">\n            {t('noMappings')}\n          </Typography>\n        )}\n        {dataMappings.map((m) => (\n          <TextField\n            key={`${m.index}-${m.value}`}\n            label={labelFor(m.value, m.header)}\n            value={values[m.index] ?? ''}\n            onChange={(e) =>\n              setValues((v) => ({...v, [m.index]: e.target.value}))\n            }\n            size=\"small\"\n            fullWidth\n            margin=\"dense\"\n            variant=\"outlined\"\n            helperText={m.header ? `column: ${m.header}` : undefined}\n          />\n        ))}\n      </DialogContent>\n      <DialogActions>\n        <Button onClick={onClose}>{t('cancel')}</Button>\n        <Button variant=\"contained\" onClick={handleSave}>\n          {t('save')}\n        </Button>\n      </DialogActions>\n    </Dialog>\n  )\n}\n"
}

### CLAUDE (2026-05-28T17:11:10.199Z)

Shipped. HMR picks it up.

**End-to-end flow:**

1. Each row on the **Jobs / Shipments / Vehicles / Depots** tabs of Input Preview now has an edit-pencil icon in a new column between the checkbox and the data columns.
2. Click the pencil → `EditRowDialog` opens with one text field per mapped column for that entity (labels translated via the existing `mapperFields` catalog the data-mapper already uses; `header` is shown as helper text under each field so the user can correlate to the original CSV column).
3. Edit any field, click **Save changes**.
4. The new `updatePreviewRow` effect (`models/input/input-core.ts`):
   - Dispatches `setRawCell` for every changed field — writing back into `inputCore[type].rawData.rows[rowIndex][col]` (or `attachedRows` when the column is in the attached range).
   - Re-runs `parseJob` / `parseShipment` / `parseVehicle` / `parseDepots` on the patched row with the existing `extraConfig` (timezone, etc.), producing a fresh parsed entity.
   - Dispatches `setOutputItem` to swap that one entity in `output[type][rowIndex]`.

**Persistence:** because the override is now part of `rawData`, it survives:
- Closing/reopening the dialog
- Switching tabs
- Saving via the existing **Save data** flow — `saveInputSet` (which Task #5 already changed to include rawData for all entity types) packs the edited rows into the saved profile, so loading the profile restores the overrides.

**Re-parse correctness:** derived structures (time-window arrays, capacities, location parsing into the canonical `"lng,lat"` string the lasso now relies on) all come from the same parser the initial import uses — no risk of drift between "originally imported" and "edited" rows.

**Caveats / next-iteration ideas:**

- All inputs are plain text fields. For numeric fields (priority, service, capacity columns) you can type any string and the parser will coerce — invalid values silently parse to `NaN`. If you want type-aware controls (numeric inputs, date pickers for time windows, lat/lng split inputs), tell me which fields and I'll specialize them.
- No "edited" badge or color tint on a row after override — easy to add if you want a visual cue.
- The lasso polygon / selection state is preserved across edits because we only touch one row.
- Multi-row bulk edit isn't there yet — the dialog handles one row at a time.

 "old_string": "    async deleteData(\n      payload: {type: InputType; indexes: number[]},\n      rootState: RootState,\n    ) {",
 "new_string": "    /**\n     * Append a new preview row from a partial set of mapped-column values.\n     *\n     * Mirrors `updatePreviewRow` for the append case:\n     *  - Allocates a fresh raw row sized to match the existing data (rows +\n     *    attachedRows) and slots the provided values at their column indexes.\n     *  - Pushes the row into rawData via `appendRawRow`.\n     *  - Re-parses through the same entry point used at load and appends the\n     *    parsed entity to `output[type]` via `appendOutputItem`.\n     *  - Auto-extends the corresponding selection list so the new row is\n     *    selected by default (matches the post-import behavior).\n     */\n    async addPreviewRow(\n      payload: {type: InputType; columnUpdates: Record<number, string>},\n      rootState: RootState,\n    ) {\n      const {type, columnUpdates} = payload\n      const state = rootState.inputCore\n      const inputSet = state[type]\n      const rowsCols = inputSet.rawData.rows[0]?.length ?? 0\n      const attachedCols = inputSet.rawData.attachedRows[0]?.length ?? 0\n      const totalCols = Math.max(\n        rowsCols + attachedCols,\n        // If the dataset is empty, infer width from the largest column\n        // index in the patch so we at least have somewhere to store it.\n        ...Object.keys(columnUpdates).map((k) => Number(k) + 1),\n        0,\n      )\n\n      const newFullRow: string[] = new Array(totalCols).fill('')\n      for (const [colIdxStr, val] of Object.entries(columnUpdates)) {\n        const idx = Number(colIdxStr)\n        if (idx >= 0 && idx < newFullRow.length) {\n          newFullRow[idx] = val\n        }\n      }\n\n      const splitAt = Math.min(rowsCols, totalCols)\n      const newRowPart = newFullRow.slice(0, splitAt)\n      const newAttachedPart = newFullRow.slice(splitAt)\n\n      dispatch.inputCore.appendRawRow({\n        type,\n        row: newRowPart,\n        attachedRow: newAttachedPart,\n      })\n\n      const extConfig = {\n        timezone: state.preferences.timezone,\n      } as extraConfig\n      const connection = state.preferences.connection\n      let parsed: any\n      if (type === 'vehicle') {\n        parsed = parseVehicle(\n          // @ts-expect-error - connection type mismatch (mirrors generateOutput)\n          connection,\n          newFullRow,\n          inputSet.mapConfig.dataMappings,\n          inputSet.mapConfig.metaMappings,\n          extConfig,\n        )\n      } else if (type === 'job') {\n        parsed = parseJob(\n          // @ts-expect-error - connection type mismatch\n          connection,\n          newFullRow,\n          inputSet.mapConfig.dataMappings,\n          inputSet.mapConfig.metaMappings,\n          extConfig,\n        )\n      } else if (type === 'shipment') {\n        parsed = parseShipment(\n          // @ts-expect-error - connection type mismatch\n          connection,\n          newFullRow,\n          inputSet.mapConfig.dataMappings,\n          inputSet.mapConfig.metaMappings,\n          extConfig,\n        )\n        if (parsed) delete parsed['metadata']\n      } else if (type === 'depot') {\n        parsed = parseDepots(\n          // @ts-expect-error - connection type mismatch\n          connection,\n          newFullRow,\n          inputSet.mapConfig.dataMappings,\n          inputSet.mapConfig.metaMappings,\n          extConfig,\n        )\n      }\n\n      if (parsed) {\n        dispatch.inputCore.appendOutputItem({type, item: parsed})\n      }\n\n      // Auto-select the appended row so the preview reflects it.\n      const newRowIndex = inputSet.rawData.rows.length // pre-append length\n      const currentSelected =\n        type === 'job'\n          ? rootState.inputPreview.selectedJobs\n          : type === 'shipment'\n            ? rootState.inputPreview.selectedShipments\n            : type === 'vehicle'\n              ? rootState.inputPreview.selectedVehicles\n              : rootState.inputPreview.selectedDepots\n      const nextSelected = [...currentSelected, newRowIndex]\n      if (type === 'job') {\n        dispatch.inputPreview.setSelectedJobs(nextSelected)\n      } else if (type === 'shipment') {\n        dispatch.inputPreview.setSelectedShipments(nextSelected)\n      } else if (type === 'vehicle') {\n        dispatch.inputPreview.setSelectedVehicles(nextSelected)\n      } else if (type === 'depot') {\n        dispatch.inputPreview.setSelectedDepots(nextSelected)\n      }\n    },\n    async deleteData(\n      payload: {type: InputType; indexes: number[]},\n      rootState: RootState,\n    ) {"
}

### CLAUDE (2026-05-28T17:20:06.600Z)

Shipped. HMR picks it up.

**End-to-end flow:**

1. On any non-Preferences preview tab (Jobs / Shipments / Vehicles / Depots), an **+** button appears in the toolbar between the tab pills and the edit/trash icons.
2. Click **+** → the `EditRowDialog` opens in **add mode** with empty inputs for every mapped column for the active entity.
3. Fill in whatever values you want (only the mapped columns are surfaced — same as the edit dialog). Click **Add**.
4. The new `addPreviewRow` effect in `input-core.ts`:
   - Allocates a fresh raw row sized to match the existing dataset's column widths (or, for an empty dataset, sized just large enough to hold the largest column index in your patch — so adding the first row to an empty Vehicles tab still works).
   - Writes provided values into the raw row, splits it back into `rows` + `attachedRows` portions, dispatches `appendRawRow`.
   - Re-runs `parseJob` / `parseShipment` / `parseVehicle` / `parseDepots` on the new row using the same `extraConfig` + `connection` as the initial import, dispatches `appendOutputItem`.
   - Auto-extends `selectedJobs` / `selectedShipments` / `selectedVehicles` / `selectedDepots` to include the new row's index — so the row is selected by default (and counted in the tab badge).
5. The new row appears at the bottom of the table, shows up on the preview map, and is included in `Generate Route` until you deselect it.

**Persistence:** like the edit case, the new row lives in `rawData.rows` + `attachedRows`. When you Save the profile, `saveInputSet` (Task #5) writes the full set including the new row. Reloading the profile restores it.

**Caveats:**

- No type-aware inputs (all fields are plain text). For numeric / time / location fields you can paste the same format you'd use in a CSV. Validation runs through the same parser, so the standard warnings will show up on the next `validateInputData` pass if the values are malformed.
- If you haven't mapped any columns for the entity yet, the dialog shows the "No mapped columns to edit." copy and the Add button is disabled-by-empty-form (clicking Add will append a blank row, which the parser will skip).
- The Add button is hidden on the Preferences tab.

{
 "file_path": "/Users/[USER]/workspace/ncc/apps/route-planner-v2/components/input/input-preview-page/address-autocomplete.tsx",
 "content": "'use client'\n/**\n * AddressAutocomplete — search field backed by NextBillion's discover\n * endpoint. Used in the row Add/Edit dialog to fill in location-typed\n * fields without making the user paste lat/lng numbers.\n *\n * Request:\n *   GET https://<map-host>/h/discover?q=<query>&limit=5&key=<apiKey>\n *\n * Response shape mirrors the BFF `/geocode/batch` items:\n *   { items: [{ title: string, id: string, position: {lat, lng}, address?: {label} }, ...] }\n *\n * The same `currentApiKey.kid` already used for map tile URLs authenticates\n * this call — no extra auth wiring needed.\n */\n\nimport {useContext, useEffect, useState} from 'react'\nimport {\n  Autocomplete,\n  CircularProgress,\n  TextField,\n} from '@mui/material'\nimport {AppContext, env} from '@ncc/common/client'\nimport {useDebounce} from 'use-debounce'\nimport {useTranslations} from 'next-intl'\n\nconst PROD_MAP_HOST = 'api.nextbillion.io'\nconst STG_MAP_HOST = 'sgpstg.nextbillion.io'\nconst MAP_HOST = env.prod() ? PROD_MAP_HOST : STG_MAP_HOST\nconst MIN_QUERY_LENGTH = 3\nconst DEBOUNCE_MS = 250\n\nexport type DiscoverItem = {\n  title: string\n  id?: string\n  position: {lat: number; lng: number}\n  address?: {label?: string}\n}\n\ntype Props = {\n  label: string\n  /** Initial textual hint to seed the input. For edit mode this is the\n   *  human-readable address if one exists; otherwise the \"lat,lng\" stub. */\n  initialInputValue?: string\n  /** Fires when the user picks a suggestion. The dialog uses this to\n   *  populate the underlying raw columns for the group. */\n  onPick: (item: DiscoverItem) => void\n}\n\nexport function AddressAutocomplete({label, initialInputValue, onPick}: Props) {\n  const [{currentApiKey}] = useContext(AppContext)\n  const t = useTranslations('editRow')\n\n  const [inputValue, setInputValue] = useState(initialInputValue ?? '')\n  const [debouncedInput] = useDebounce(inputValue, DEBOUNCE_MS)\n  const [options, setOptions] = useState<DiscoverItem[]>([])\n  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false)\n  const [value, setValue] = useState<DiscoverItem | null>(null)\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    const query = debouncedInput.trim()\n    if (query.length < MIN_QUERY_LENGTH || !currentApiKey?.kid) {\n      setOptions([])\n      setLoading(false)\n      return\n    }\n    // Don't refetch when the user already picked a value whose title matches\n    // the current input verbatim — otherwise picking a suggestion would\n    // immediately reissue a search for the same string.\n    if (value && value.title === query) {\n      return\n    }\n    const controller = new AbortController()\n    setLoading(true)\n    const url = `https://${MAP_HOST}/h/discover?q=${encodeURIComponent(\n      query,\n    )}&limit=5&key=${encodeURIComponent(currentApiKey.kid)}`\n    fetch(url, {signal: controller.signal})\n      .then((r) => (r.ok ? r.json() : Promise.reject(r)))\n      .then((data) => {\n        const items: DiscoverItem[] = Array.isArray(data?.items)\n          ? data.items\n          : []\n        setOptions(items)\n      })\n      .catch((err) => {\n        if (controller.signal.aborted) return\n        // Surface the error to console; user just sees an empty option list.\n        // eslint-disable-next-line no-console\n        console.warn('[AddressAutocomplete] discover request failed', err)\n        setOptions([])\n      })\n      .finally(() => {\n        if (!controller.signal.aborted) setLoading(false)\n      })\n    return () => controller.abort()\n  }, [debouncedInput, currentApiKey?.kid, value])\n\n  return (\n    <Autocomplete<DiscoverItem, false, false, true>\n      freeSolo\n      filterOptions={(x) => x} // server-filtered\n      options={options}\n      value={value}\n      onChange={(_, picked) => {\n        if (picked && typeof picked !== 'string') {\n          setValue(picked)\n          onPick(picked)\n        } else {\n          setValue(null)\n        }\n      }}\n      inputValue={inputValue}\n      onInputChange={(_, next, reason) => {\n        if (reason === 'reset') return\n        setInputValue(next)\n      }}\n      getOptionLabel={(option) =>\n        typeof option === 'string'\n          ? option\n          : option.address?.label ?? option.title ?? ''\n      }\n      loading={loading}\n      loadingText={`${t('addressSearch')}…`}\n      noOptionsText={\n        inputValue.trim().length < MIN_QUERY_LENGTH\n          ? t('addressSearch')\n          : t('addressNoResults')\n      }\n      isOptionEqualToValue={(a, b) => a.id === b.id || a.title === b.title}\n      renderInput={(params) => (\n        <TextField\n          {...params}\n          label={label}\n          size=\"small\"\n          fullWidth\n          margin=\"dense\"\n          variant=\"outlined\"\n          InputProps={{\n            ...params.InputProps,\n            endAdornment: (\n              <>\n                {loading ? <CircularProgress size={16} /> : null}\n                {params.InputProps.endAdornment}\n              </>\n            ),\n          }}\n        />\n      )}\n    />\n  )\n}\n"
}

{
 "replace_all": false,
 "file_path": "/Users/[USER]/workspace/ncc/apps/route-planner-v2/components/input/input-preview-page/edit-row-dialog.tsx",
 "old_string": "  const [values, setValues] = useState<Record<number, string>>({})",
 "new_string": "  const optionsMap = useMemo(\n    () => (type ? getOptionsMap(type) : ({} as Record<string, DataMapOption>)),\n    [type],\n  )\n\n  // Split mappings into:\n  //   - locationGroups: mapped columns whose option carries a location-typed\n  //     `type` (LocationLatLng / LocationLngLat / LocationLat / LocationLng /\n  //     Address). Grouped by the option's `extra.parent` so e.g. a column\n  //     for \"Lat\" and a column for \"Lng\" both end up in the same `location`\n  //     group and one autocomplete pick fills both.\n  //   - plainMappings: everything else (description, service time, etc.) —\n  //     still rendered as bare text fields.\n  const {locationGroups, plainMappings} = useMemo(() => {\n    const groups = new Map<\n      string,\n      {mappings: typeof dataMappings}\n    >()\n    const plain: typeof dataMappings = []\n    for (const m of dataMappings) {\n      const opt = optionsMap[m.value]\n      const isLocation = opt && LOCATION_TYPES.has(opt.type as MapInputType)\n      if (!isLocation) {\n        plain.push(m)\n        continue\n      }\n      const parent =\n        (opt?.extra?.parent as string | undefined) ??\n        // Fall back to stripping the `#suffix` from the value (e.g.\n        // `pickup.location#latLng` → `pickup.location`).\n        m.value.split('#')[0]\n      if (!groups.has(parent)) groups.set(parent, {mappings: []})\n      groups.get(parent)!.mappings.push(m)\n    }\n    return {\n      locationGroups: Array.from(groups.entries()).map(([parent, g]) => ({\n        parent,\n        mappings: g.mappings,\n      })),\n      plainMappings: plain,\n    }\n  }, [dataMappings, optionsMap])\n\n  const [values, setValues] = useState<Record<number, string>>({})"
}

### CLAUDE (2026-05-28T17:27:12.481Z)

Shipped. HMR picks it up.

**Summary of changes:**

- **`apps/route-planner-v2/components/input/input-preview-page/address-autocomplete.tsx`** (new): debounced (250 ms) MUI Autocomplete that calls `GET https://<map-host>/h/discover?q=&limit=5&key=<apiKey>`. Uses the same `currentApiKey.kid` from `AppContext` that the map tiles already use, and the same `api.nextbillion.io` / `sgpstg.nextbillion.io` host switching as `map-style.ts`. Aborts in-flight requests when the input changes. Shows a spinner while loading and translation-aware empty / no-results copy.

- **`apps/route-planner-v2/components/input/input-preview-page/edit-row-dialog.tsx`**:
  - Imports `JOB/VEHICLE/SHIPMENT/DEPOT_OPTIONS_MAP` to look up each mapping's `type` and `extra.parent`.
  - Splits `dataMappings` into two buckets via `useMemo`:
    - **Location groups** — mappings whose option type is `LocationLatLng / LocationLngLat / LocationLat / LocationLng / Address`, grouped by `extra.parent` (e.g. all `pickup.location#*` mappings land in one `pickup.location` group; a job's combined or separated lat/lng mappings land in one `location` group).
    - **Plain mappings** — everything else, rendered as text fields exactly like before.
  - Each location group renders **one `<AddressAutocomplete>`** with a parent-derived label (Pickup address / Delivery address / Start address / End address / Address). On pick, writes the right format to each grouped column:
    - `LocationLatLng` → `"lat,lng"` string
    - `LocationLngLat` → `"lng,lat"` string
    - `LocationLat` → bare lat
    - `LocationLng` → bare lng
    - `Address` → the formatted address string (`address.label || title`)
  - When the dialog opens in edit mode, the autocomplete is seeded with the existing Address column value if one exists, otherwise a "lat, lng" stub from the coordinate columns.

- **Catalog (en / pt-BR / es-MX)** — `editRow.addressLabel`, `editRow.addressLabel_pickup/delivery/start/end`, `editRow.addressSearch`, `editRow.addressNoResults`.

**Behavior notes:**

- Lat/lng text fields are now **hidden whenever the user has mapped any location column**. The autocomplete handles them. If you ever want to *clear* a location via the UI, just type in the autocomplete and pick a different result, or leave it untouched in edit mode.
- If the user mapped both a coordinate column AND an Address column under the same parent (uncommon but valid), the single autocomplete fills both — coords from `position`, address from `address.label`.
- The discover endpoint returns whatever the configured plan supports. If `position` is missing on a particular result (very rare), the pick will silently no-op for coordinate columns — defensive handling avoids `NaN` strings landing in the raw row.
- If the user's API key isn't authorized for the discover endpoint, the autocomplete will show "No matches" and a warning logs to console. Falls back gracefully — no error toast.
